summary: The source contract limits word length to at most ten and fixes the alphabet at 26 letters, so neighbor generation has constant legal work per dictionary word. An unseen dictionary word can change reachability or the shortest distance, giving a matching Omega(N) lower bound.

optimality.argument: In the worst case, an uninspected dictionary word can be the only missing link in a ladder or create a shorter ladder, so exact computation requires Omega(N) dictionary inspection. Because every legal word has at most ten positions and each position has only 25 different lowercase replacements, the candidate performs bounded work per visited word. Each word is enqueued at most once, giving O(N) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: An unseen dictionary word can change either target reachability or the minimum ladder length, forcing worst-case inspection of all N words.
With L <= 10 and a fixed 26-letter alphabet, each dequeued word generates at most 250 constant-size substitutions and is dequeued only once.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a reachable shortest ladder and an absent target; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
